findings.issue: Reproduced the exact contention-class flake the builder's own friction_events already documented (and correctly diagnosed): a fresh, independent full `npx vitest run` of the web/ suite (114 files) FAILED — the new 'a KC NAME_INVALID_CHARACTERS 400...' test timed out at 15000ms under full-suite parallel CPU load (file itself took 23956ms wall-clock with contention), leaving 2887/2888 not 2888/2888. An immediate re-run of the identical full suite passed clean at 114/114 files, 2888/2888. Solo, the file is reliably fast (2/2 in 1963ms total, ~1787ms for the slow test — ~8x margin under the 15000ms budget). This is the SAME systemic class already recorded as durable project lore (memory: 'конкур-нагрузка амплифицирует таймауты→валидация СОЛО') and already independently observed by the builder on the pre-existing, untouched screen-record-detail.mount.test.jsx. Not a logic defect in the new test or the fix — purely dev-machine worker-contention variance. The pr-handoff.json gate line 'web_full_suite: GREEN — 2888/2888' is accurate for a typical run but is not a deterministic guarantee; judge's own two full runs went 1-fail-then-1-pass.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking (matches T-0757.review.json R-1 precedent for the identical flake class on this same codebase). Optional systemic follow-up, out of scope for T-0748 itself: raise the global mount-test timeout class or reduce full-suite worker parallelism, tracked separately rather than re-litigated per new mount test file.

findings.issue: Live-probed a case explicitly OUT of this task's stated scope (spec.md §7 'Out of scope' only disclaims re-implementing the character set, not the length validator): an over-length firstName (300 chars, single-token display_name so splitDisplayName duplicates it into both firstName and lastName) produces a live KC 400 body `{"field":"firstName","errorMessage":"error-invalid-length-too-long",...}` — this messageKey does NOT contain the substring 'person-name', so isPersonNameCharacterError correctly returns false and the request falls through to the UNCHANGED EMAIL_INVALID default (exactly as designed — no false positive). But that means the SAME class of bug this task fixes (a firstName/lastName-caused 400 misattributed as an email problem) still reproduces for KC's length validator, not just its character validator. Practically low-risk: web/src/screens/users-form.js's own client-side DISPLAY_NAME_MAX=256 caps display_name length before it ever reaches the server, and it takes a single-TOKEN (no-space) display_name near that 256-char boundary to exceed KC's independent 255-char per-field cap (a two-word name of the same total length splits the load across firstName+lastName and stays under 255 each). Pre-existing since T-0741 (unchanged by this diff either direction — this exact messageKey already fell to EMAIL_INVALID before T-0748 and still does after).
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking follow-up candidate, not required for T-0748: extend extractKcFieldErrors' consumer to also disambiguate error-invalid-length* on firstName/lastName (or tighten DISPLAY_NAME_MAX to KC's 255 boundary for the no-space case) — narrow edge case, out of this task's stated scope (§7), and not a regression introduced here.
